title: Closing the Gap: Test and Learn
file_title: Closing the gap: test and learn - digital applications case studies
description: This document describes an evaluation of the "Closing the Gap: Test and Learn" program, which was designed to improve educational outcomes for disadvantaged children through a series of interventions. The program's goals included identifying effective educational strategies, fostering connections between teaching and research, and promoting teacher involvement in research. A range of methodological approaches, including large-scale randomized controlled trials, was employed to assess the impact of interventions on literacy and numeracy. The findings revealed mixed results, with some interventions showing potential benefits, while others did not significantly outperform standard school practices. The evaluation also highlighted the importance of teacher-led research and provided training to enhance educators' research skills. Despite some limitations, such as the reliability of standardized tests and small sample sizes, the program demonstrated the value of evidence-based practices in reducing educational disparities. The document concludes with a call for careful consideration of system-led research approaches and the interpretation of educational RCTs, along with a glossary and summaries of completed studies.

title: Teaching Schools Evaluation Final Report
description: This document describes an evaluation of the UK's Teaching School Programme and Teaching School Alliances (TSAs), which aim to create a self-improving school system by fostering collaboration and excellence among schools. The evaluation uses mixed methods, including case studies, surveys, and data analysis, to assess the effectiveness, impact, and challenges of these initiatives. It finds that teaching schools and TSAs have made progress in enhancing staff development, leadership capacity, and student outcomes, but face issues with financial sustainability, governance, and engaging schools in need. The report highlights the importance of leadership, strategic partnerships, and government support in the success of these programs. It also notes the evolving nature of TSAs, their varied regional representation, and the complexity of their operational aspects. The evaluation concludes that while TSAs are contributing positively to educational standards, their impact is complex and varies across regions, with further investigation needed into their operational details.

title: The Impact of National College Grants Evaluation
file_title: Impact of National College grants evaluation
description: This document describes an evaluation of the effectiveness of various grants provided by the National College for Teaching and Leadership (NCTL) aimed at fostering a self-improving education system in England from 2009-2013. The grants were designed to improve school leadership and encourage inter-school support. Sheffield Hallam University's multi-phase evaluation, which included surveys, interviews, and case studies, found that the grants generally enhanced leadership capacity, confidence, and practice, particularly noting the impact of Succession Planning Grants on career progression. While the grants positively influenced school leadership and teaching capacity, improvements in pupil outcomes were less evident. The evaluation concluded that grant success depended on factors such as quality support, trust, systematic change, and local collaboration. Recommendations for future grant initiatives include clear objectives, consistent impact data collection, and alignment with school needs. The document also notes that the views expressed are those of the authors and not necessarily government policy, with the full report available on the government website.
